reason: Under the value lens the expected public gain is about +0.0005, well below the +0.002 bar. (1) Ceiling: the idea caps it at the authors' own scores minus our base, i.e. 0.959-0.953 = +0.006 (Tennant) and 0.956-0.953 = +0.003 (Pothula) (browser_research_2026-09-24_pass2.md l.110-111). Both authors publish BELOW their own score, though. Pothula released x138 at 0.953 while his team was at 0.956. Tennant's newest public kernel (readmit-v1, 0.946, 19 Sep) sits 0.013 under his 0.959 (browser_research_2026-09-24.md l.118-121). Both are in the silver zone (ranks 32 and 58 of 3,872 teams; silver is roughly the top ~190). Publishing their best lets copy-plus-rider teams pass them. So a realistic release is at most about their score minus 0.003: ~0.953-0.954 from Pothula (nothing new over x138) and <= ~0.956 from Tennant. (2) Selection and noise: a team score is the MAX over many public submissions on ONE embryo. Byte-identical public notebooks scored 0.946 and 0.942 (discussions_summary.md l.101,128). A +0.003 best-of-N public gap therefore shrinks to about +0.001..+0.002 of expected true gain. (3) Private transfer: private is 71% and made of other, unseen embryos. Public-selected post-processing transfers at roughly 0.5x (lab +0.0019 -> LB +0.001; filters that were +0.01 in the lab were 0 on the LB, BRIEF s.1). Unlike x138's head, which had a held-out-by-movie check, a successor tuned on public comes with no transfer evidence. Tennant's 0.959 is most likely built without V1284 (h_kaggle-intel.json), so even his lever is untested on an x138 base. (4) Gate attrition: our own adoption gate (>= max(#34,#35)+0.002 with LB noise 0.003) passes a true +0.002 successor only about half the time. E[public] = P(release >= 0.954 by 28 Sep) ~0.2-0.3 (a guess) x E[gain | release] ~+0.002 x P(gate) ~0.5 ~= +0.0003..+0.0006. E[private] is about half that. The idea itself says +0.001 before these discounts. A WebSearch found no new author notebook indexed; kaggle.com cannot be reached from here (browser_todo). As an option it costs little, but as a value line it does not clear +0.002 and has no transfer evidence.
fix_if_any: Downgrade it from a planned line to a zero-cost watch with hard triggers. No agent or GPU time is reserved unless a trigger fires. Browser sweeps at 06:00 UTC on 26, 27 and 28 Sep (Code tab sorted by score; the thtennant and anvithpothula kernel lists; the LB histogram for a new spike at >= 0.955). Port ONLY IF all of these hold: (a) the public notebook's own score is >= 0.956, i.e. >= base +0.003, clear of LB noise, and ideally confirmed by a new copy spike of >= 10 teams at that score; (b) it uses only public, attachable datasets and fits a 12 h run including x138's REPAIR_DEADLINE_S guard; (c) its diff against exp56 is small and explainable (one or two mechanisms, as with x138's head), not a sweep of knobs. Prefer a Tennant release to Pothula's: his lever is probably orthogonal to V1284, so diff-porting ONLY that lever onto x138 (+ divinsert) is the valuable variant. For transfer, run the successor's built-in VALIDATOR on train movies of BOTH embryos (44b6 and 6bba separately) and require no drop versus exp56 on either. The check is in-sample for the networks, but relink/readmit-type post-processing does not lean on network confidence, so it is informative. Only after that should it enter the finals, and never as F1 on a public tie.
realistic_public_gain: +0.0005 expected (range 0 to +0.003; +0.006 only if Tennant publishes his full 0.959 chain, which his publishing history makes unlikely). Conditional on a qualifying release: about +0.002.
realistic_private_gain: +0.0002..+0.0003 expected (about 0.5x the public gain for public-selected post-processing; could be negative if the successor was selected on the public embryo). Conditional on release: about +0.001.
critical_path: Only if a trigger fires. User's browser sweep 26 Sep 06:00 UTC (also 27 and 28 Sep) -> agent-container: kernels-pull output triaged, cell-by-cell diff vs experiments/exp56_x138_verbatim, verbatim copy through build_probe_kernel --base <successor> (1-2 h, by ~09:00) -> kaggle-vitalii: private dummy-test run on 4 clips after the 26 Sep 00:00 GPU reset (15-40 min, ~10:00) -> Vitalii submits with the user's OK (~10:30) -> scored ~17:30-20:30 UTC. The last trigger that can still inform the finals is a release seen by ~28 Sep 22:00 UTC, so the submission goes in by 29 Sep 10:00 UTC. Unconditionally, P(something to score) is only ~0.2-0.3.
